sources.title: Elisabeth A. Hildebrand and Steven A. Brandt, An Archaeological Survey of the Tropical Highlands of Kafa, Southwestern Ethiopia (2010)
sources.note: Author-uploaded original article read in full through web extraction, Journal of African Archaeology 8(1), 43 to 63; DOI 10.3213/1612-1651-10152. Regional distinctions, uneven research coverage and local kingdoms support the cautious regional scope. Imported dates and bounds are independently decoded atlas metadata.

sources.title: John W. Arthur and colleagues, The Transition from Hunting to Gathering to Food Production in the Gamo Highlands of Southern Ethiopia (2019)
sources.note: Original open-access excavation article read directly. Pre-pottery and early pottery sections distinguish hunting, pottery, barley and later livestock. Single early barley grain could not be directly dated; contextual association is expressly qualified. No ethnic/genetic continuity inferred.

sources.title: Hildebrand, Brandt and Lesur-Gebremariam, The Holocene Archaeology of Southwest Ethiopia: New Insights from the Kafa Archaeological Project (2010)
sources.note: Original article read in full in its author-uploaded ResearchGate copy, https://www.researchgate.net/publication/226118825_The_Holocene_Archaeology_of_Southwest_Ethiopia_New_Insights_from_the_Kafa_Archaeological_Project. Printed pages 268 to 269: Kumali caprine/cattle evidence and plant remains; suspicious much older cattle date rejected by authors. Leaves cannot yet distinguish Musa from wild/domestic Ensete.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Tiya: Prehistoric site
sources.note: Direct official project account read. Describes cemetery with stelae erected between tenth and fifteenth centuries, graves, swords and enigmatic signs. Main listing retains less precise legacy description; broad date range used, not exact founding year. Tiya is inside both decoded polygons.

sources.title: Bertrand Poissonnier, Restauration des sites à stèles décorées de Tuto Fela et Tiya, Annales d’Ethiopie 16 (2000), 25 to 34
sources.note: Author-uploaded original article read in web extraction. Figure 1, page 25, dates manual re-erection of Tiya stele 2 to April 1998; figure 9, page 32, shows repair of stele 34. Used as dated conservation evidence, not medieval construction technique.

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, The Gedeo Cultural Landscape
sources.note: Direct official listing read; inscription in 2023. Multilayer agroforestry and living knowledge, not evidence that every aspect existed in 1500 BCE or 700 CE.

sources.title: Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew, The false banana (2018)
sources.note: Direct institutional account read. Enset food processing, kocho, bulla and amicho; explicitly modern documented example. No claim to know first domestication date.

sources.title: John W. Arthur, Transforming Clay: Gamo Caste, Gender, and Pottery of Southwestern Ethiopia (2013)
sources.note: Original African Study Monographs Supplement 46, pages 5 to 25, read directly. Main fieldwork September 1996 to April 1998; learning pages 12 to 13, family labor pages 9 to 11 and 14, polishing heirlooms page 17. Modern ethnography not projected into archaeological map intervals.

sources.title: Yvonne Treis, Ideophones in Kambaata (Cushitic): Grammar, meaning and use (2024)
sources.note: Original open-access journal PDF read directly, printed pages 147 to 200. Exact sample éman and gloss congratulations! at printed page 152, PDF page 6. Table 2 on printed page 156 gives húf=y- with meanings boiling over or rising through fermentation. Latin-based official orthography with added stress accents is explained in section 2; no ancient writing claim.

proposedOverrides.name: Communities of the central and southwestern Ethiopian highlands
proposedOverrides.summary: A regional history of varied highland livelihoods, with ancient finds and clearly dated living traditions.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Overlapping broad central/southwestern regions allow a shared regional narrative with distinct map phases. Bounds match, but decoded polygons differ: the 700 CE shape has a substantial northern indentation. These are not aliases of one dynasty, not all ethnic groups given one identity, and not Aksum/Yeha, which lie north of both polygons. Agriculture did not begin simultaneously at the imported first date.
batchIdentityNotes.writing: Attested modern Kambaata éman, congratulations!, in Treis 2024, printed page 152, PDF page 6. Exact Latin-based scholarly spelling; not a fabricated ancient highland language or an invented Ethiopic transliteration.
batchIdentityNotes.limits: Core case studies Mota, Kafa, Tiya and Kambaata lie within the Ethiopian highland portion. Gedeo falls southeast of the true sloping polygon edge despite being within its bounding box, and is explicitly neighbouring context. Mota fish evidence is earlier than the first interval; Kumali lies between map phases; medieval Tiya and all modern examples are labelled as later.
